operators.name: embedding1_forward
semantics: Gather rows from weight according to input indices: output[i,j,k] = weight[input[i,j], k].
Input shape [B, L], weight shape [E, D], output shape [B, L, D].
Input values are in range [0, E-1].
Output is created via torch::empty with shape [B, L, D] on CUDA.

operators.name: embedding2_forward
semantics: Gather rows from weight according to input indices: output[i,j,k] = weight[input[i,j], k].
Input shape [B, L], weight shape [E, D], output shape [B, L, D].
Input values are in range [0, E-1].
Output is created via torch::empty with shape [B, L, D] on CUDA.

operators.name: add_tensors
semantics: Both tensors have identical shape [B, L, D].
Output is allocated with torch::empty_like(a) (or b).
self.embedding1(x1) returns a float32 CUDA tensor of shape [2048, 512, 64] by gathering from embedding1.weight using x1 indices.
self.embedding2(x2) returns a float32 CUDA tensor of shape [2048, 512, 64] by gathering from embedding2.weight using x2 indices.
The two embeddings are added elementwise, resulting in a float32 CUDA tensor of shape [2048, 512, 64].
The addition is plain tensor addition with no scaling, no bias, and broadcasting is not needed because shapes are identical.
